transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-04-07
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Aisha (ParcelEase Head of ML), Tom (Infra), Maya (PM)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in to review Dedicated sizing options and autoscaling/burst planning. Action items captured.

[00:00] Jesse: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — sizing review, autoscale policy, soak/bench plan and next steps. priya will lead the perf stuff.
[00:20] Aisha: thanks. our main ask is predictable latency at peak shopping hours, and we want to limit cost. current POC running on hosted but we saw spikes last week so evaluating Dedicated.
[00:38] Priya: got it. can you remind us of target SLOs? p95 under 350ms for single-turn chat generation?
[00:48] Maya: yes p95 350, p99 under 700 if possible. cost target is under $0.006 per 1k tokens generated ideally but that's flexible.
[01:05] Tom: also important — we need burst for marketing campaigns: sustained 3-5 minute spikes up to ~200 RPS, baseline 40 RPS.
[01:20] Priya: ok that's helpful. quick note — Dedicated pools autoscale on GPU tasks by adding nodes based on queued requests and avg latency. we usually recommend a min pool sized for baseline and rapid scale for bursts with short cooldowns.
[01:40] Aisha: baseline conversation we had earlier — what does min capacity translate to in GPUs?
[01:48] Priya: with your model (redwood-curie-equivalent open-xx model, 8B) we saw ~12 tokens/sec per A100 equivalent for 16k context in our test; your avg token length and prompt/response ratio matter. using your token distro from last week — median request ~220 tokens total — I'd map baseline 40 RPS to 2 x A100 equiv nodes to keep p95 headroom.
[02:15] Tom: wait when you say A100 equiv, our infra team uses different GPU types. also curious about cold starts when adding nodes.
[02:28] Priya: yeah, cold-start is real. adding a brand new node and warming can take ~30–90s depending on model and kv cache. we mitigate with warm-buffer capacity (burst pool) and pre-warmed standby nodes. recommend min nodes + a small warm buffer 1 node for your traffic pattern.
[02:52] Jesse: for pricing and commit — if you need 2 min nodes + 1 warm buffer and burst up to 6 nodes for campaign windows, that's what we should size in the Dedicated proposal.
[03:08] Aisha: what about autoscale cooldowns? if there's repeated short spikes, we don't want oscillation.
[03:18] Priya: good point. cooldown and scale-step matters. set aggressive scale-up (short window, small percent) and conservative scale-down (longer cooldown e.g., 120–300s) to avoid flapping. you can configure max scale step to add multiple nodes quickly during a big spike.
[03:38] Tom: how does prefix/K V cache affect cold start? we have common prompts and repeated prefixes for product lookups.
[03:46] Priya: prefix / KV cache reduces work per token significantly. if the cache is warm on the node you scale to, cold-starts are faster because less compute per step; but cache is node-local in Dedicated, so newly-added nodes won't have warm cache. we can use sticky routing to keep similar sessions on warmed nodes, or reserve cache-warmed standby nodes.
[04:12] Maya: sticky routing — does that impact load balancing fairness?
[04:18] Priya: some, but you can do affinity for session groups — we balance latency vs utilization. for campaigns with predictable keys, affinity helps.
[04:27] Aisha: any change to model quantization or size suggested? we're currently running float16.
[04:33] Priya: float16 is fine. quantization to int8 or 4-bit helps density but can affect output quality. for POC we recommend keep fp16, validate quantized profile in a separate run if cost pressure remains.
[04:48] Jesse: ok let's talk concrete numbers: baseline 40 RPS -> 2 nodes + 1 warm buffer. Burst target 200 RPS -> scale to 6 nodes. Cooldown scale-down 180–300s. Does that align?
[05:05] Tom: sounds reasonable but need to validate with soak.
[05:08] Priya: we'll run a 2-hour soak simulating baseline+regular small spikes and a scheduled full-burst window to measure p95/p99 and util. we'll instrument GPU util, queue length, latencies.
[05:26] Aisha: can you simulate our 95th percentile token lengths? ours has long tails during returns processing.
[05:33] Jesse: remind me, you sent a token distribution file last week — if you can re-send Tom, Priya can feed it into the sizing calc.
[05:44] Tom: yep will send last 30 days. note our peak-minute logs are in Datadog; I'll export.
[05:50] Priya: perfect — that lets us map tokens/sec to GPU need accurately.
[05:55] Maya: on billing — if we scale to 6 nodes for 5 minutes, how does burst billing work?
[06:02] Jesse: Dedicated billing is based on committed nodes + burst usage pricing. bursts are billed at slightly higher per-minute rate; we'll include example cost for your projected burst minutes in the pricing sheet.
[06:14] Aisha: ok good. what's the expected p99 during burst if cache is cold?
[06:19] Priya: with cold cache and new nodes added, p99 can jump a lot — sometimes 2–4x baseline. that's why warm buffer and sticky routing help. our soak will capture that delta.
[06:34] Tom: any best-practices for request shaping to help scale? e.g., queueing some non-critical requests or rate-limiting marketing campaign traffic?
[06:44] Priya: yes, triage policies work: route high-priority traffic to dedicated pool, and fallback for lower-priority to hosted or lower-cost model. Redwood supports policy routing by route tags.
[06:58] Maya: if we run a canary during the campaign, can Redwood do automatic fallback to hosted model if Dedicated is saturated?
[07:06] Jesse: yes — you can configure automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in another pool/region. it's part of the rollout/fallback policy.
[07:14] Aisha: security quick check — we need SOC2 and audit logs for Dedicated, SSO integration.
[07:20] Jesse: we have SOC2 + can provide audit log exports; Dedicated supports SAML SSO/SCIM and KMS integration. we'll attach the security doc.
[07:30] Tom: one more infra question — network egress if we run private deployment? not in scope for this POC but curious.
[07:36] Priya: for Private we support VPC peering and on-prem with no egress; Dedicated still has customer isolation but uses our managed infra — egress rules can be controlled via connectors. we can loop in infra docs.
[07:48] Aisha: ok next steps recap please.
[07:51] Jesse: priya will run soak and share results; i'll send pricing + sizing calc; tom will send RPS/token logs; maya to confirm decision stakeholders; schedule benchmark next week with steady 100 RPS and 200 RPS bursts.
[08:06] Priya: planning notes — soak config: baseline 40 RPS for 90 mins, then burst window 10 minutes at 200 RPS, repeat, capture metrics. we'll push logs to the shared drive.
[08:20] Tom: do you need our test keys or will you run against a synthetic workload?
[08:24] Priya: synthetic but with your token distro. if you want end-to-end we'll use test keys but prefer not to use production.
[08:33] Maya: please include cost projection scenarios in the doc.
[08:36] Jesse: will do.
[08:38] Aisha: ok thanks everyone. if performance after soak looks good we can move toward a Reserved capacity commit.
[08:45] Jesse: great. we'll follow up by EOD with docs and target the benchmark early next week. thanks all.

End transcript. Notes: occasional transcription glitches: "K V" for KV, sometimes names garbled (Maya/Maiya). Speakers labeled by first name, minor filler words retained.
